"Not a deadline" on a Due chip: the conversation's deadline decisions become rejected. They
leave has:deadline and the chip, and a re-run of triage does not add them again. With sender,

get.description:
Every sidebar number in one answer: {cursor, views: {view: {unread,
total}}, inbox_count, waiting, approvals, failed}. Each view is counted with the conditions
its list uses, so a number always equals the length of the list it opens. The live stream
sends the same object as a `counts` event after each change.

The number by Inbox in the sidebar. With the `inbox_count`
setting "first_tab" (default) it is the unread conversations the active layout's first tab
lists: Primary in the Default layout, the whole inbox list in a layout with one tab, the
first tab of a custom layout. Mail that other tabs claim is left out; those tabs show their
own counts. With "all" it is every unread conversation with the Inbox label, as the Inbox
label's own count in GET /labels.

What each tab shows by its label, counted in one query for the whole layout.

Without `detail` (older clients): {tab_id: n}, the count of the tab's `badge`. With
`detail`: {"tabs": {tab_id: {...}}} with, for each of the tab's indicators, `unread`
(counting stops at 1000, shown as "999+"), `all` (counting stops at 200,000, shown
as "200,000+") and for "due" `due_count`, `earliest_due` (a date), `earliest_due_cid`,
`earliest_due_from` and `earliest_due_subject`. "due" counts deadlines from MAILR_OVERDUE_DAYS
ago (default 7) on. Every count covers the tab's sections
together and leaves out what a claiming tab takes. The first tab's unread is not capped: it
is the sidebar's Inbox count (GET /inbox/count, `first_tab_unread`).

The message body for the reader. It changes nothing: no read flag, no receipt, no audit
entry for a session (only tokens are audited), so the web app may prefetch it.
The grid: Notes (not archived), Lists, Archive, Trash, Reminders or one label's notes.

Tasks from the mirror. `smart`: today, overdue, upcoming, scheduled, nodate (no_date),
high, email, all, completed (server-defined, so every client shows the same rows); rows of
Today and Upcoming carry `section`. `q` takes the search operators (list:, tag: or @tag,
due:<fri, is:done, is:overdue, has:email, pri:high).
Open tasks per smart list, per list (by URL; `lists_by_id` by calendar_id) and per tag.
